prompts.display_text: Pin a country with ten or more of the Church's missions (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with ten or more of the Church's missions (end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Guatemala, Japan, Ecuador and DR Congo with 7 each.
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 the United States had 120 of the Church's missions. Brazil (37), Mexico (34) and the Philippines (26) came next, and Peru, Argentina, Chile and Nigeria had 11 or more each. Nigeria and the Philippines were the only countries outside the Americas with ten or more.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in Josiah's reforms, his death at Megiddo, or Pharaoh Necho's march
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place or kingdom named in Josiah's reforms and death and their aftermath (2 Kings 23; 2 Chronicles 35:20-36:4): Bethel and Samaria's high places, Megiddo, Necho's march against the king of Assyria toward Carchemish by Euphrates, Riblah in Hamath, and Egypt
prompts.note: Bethel and Samaria are in the West Bank (Palestine); Megiddo is in Israel.
prompts.summary: King Josiah of Judah purged idolatry from Jerusalem to Bethel and the cities of Samaria. When Pharaoh Necho marched north toward Carchemish to aid the king of Assyria, Josiah met him at Megiddo and was slain. Necho then bound Josiah's son Jehoahaz at Riblah and carried him to Egypt (2 Kgs 23; 2 Chr 35).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Pharaoh-nechoh king of Egypt came up, and he carried Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died (2 Kgs 23:29, 34).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Josiah went against Necho and was slain at Megiddo (2 Kgs 23:29; 2 Chr 35:22-24).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Josiah broke down the altar at Bethel and the high places in the cities of Samaria (2 Kgs 23:15, 19).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Necho put Jehoahaz in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath (2 Kgs 23:33).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Necho came to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates (2 Chr 35:20); the ruins of Carchemish lie at Turkey's border with Syria; Church Bible Maps 5, 6 and 9 plot Carchemish on the upper Euphrates.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding part of the Jordan River, the sea of Chinnereth, or the Hermon springs that feed it
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding part of the Jordan River, the river Israel crossed under Joshua and Naaman washed in, including its sea of Chinnereth (Galilee) and the springs of Mount Hermon that feed it
prompts.note: Mount Hermon sits on the Lebanon-Syria border, and its springs feed the Jordan, so both count, as in the Song of Solomon prompt.
prompts.summary: The Jordan River gathers springs on the slopes of Mount Hermon, flows through the sea of Chinnereth (Galilee), and winds down to the salt sea. Israel crossed it on dry ground at Jericho under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha parted it, and Naaman the Syrian was healed by dipping in it seven times (Josh 3; 2 Kgs 2, 5).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: The Jordan runs through the sea of Chinnereth, the Sea of Galilee, which lies in Israel (Deut 3:17; Bible Dictionary, Jordan River).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: The river forms Jordan's western border; Israel camped on its east bank before crossing (Josh 3:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The lower river near Jericho, where the waters stood up as an heap for Israel, borders the West Bank (Josh 3:16).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The Bible Dictionary says the Jordan is formed by several springs rising in Mount Hermon, a mountain on the Syria-Lebanon border.

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Those Hermon springs feed the Jordan, and Mount Hermon's western slopes lie in Lebanon (Bible Dictionary, Jordan River and Hermon).

prompts.display_text: Pin a men's FIFA World Cup winning country with a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: A country whose men's national team has won the FIFA World Cup (through 2022) and that has a temple dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology; FIFA World Cup records
prompts.summary: Every men's World Cup winner has a temple as of October 2026. Brazil, Argentina, Germany, Italy, France, Spain and England (United Kingdom) all have dedicated temples, and Uruguay, the first champion in 1930, dedicated its Montevideo temple in 2001.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Three titles, latest 2022; Buenos Aires temple (1986).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Four titles; Freiberg (1985) and Frankfurt (1987) temples.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: England won in 1966; London (1958) and Preston (1998) temples.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Spanish-speaking country where the Church has 10 to 19 stakes as of October 2026.
prompts.text_original: A Spanish-speaking country where the Church has between 10 and 19 stakes as of October 2026 (year-end 2025 figures).
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025), read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Most Spanish-speaking countries have either 20 or more stakes (Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Guatemala and others) or fewer than 10 (Panama, Cuba, Equatorial Guinea). Five sit in between: Uruguay (18), Spain (17), Nicaragua (12), Paraguay (11) and Costa Rica (10). Puerto Rico, a territory, has 5.
